subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

In those days, we did not expect luxuries; we were thankful if we could __keep the wolf from the door__.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"keep the wolf from the door"** means to avoid starvation or financial ruin; it implies managing to survive with the basic necessities. (भुखमरी से बचना)

 
 
• **Example:** During the recession, many families struggled to keep the wolf from the door.
 
 
 
• **"Avoid starvation"** means ensuring that one has enough food to survive, preventing hunger. (भुखमरी से बचना)
 
 
• **Example:** They worked hard to avoid starvation during the drought.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Avoid starvation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Wallow in poverty** (गरीबी में डूबना): To live in a state of extreme poverty and make no effort to improve the situation.

 
 
• **Example:** Instead of wallowing in poverty, they sought ways to improve their living conditions.
 
 
 
• **Relish food** (भोजन का आनंद लेना): To enjoy or take pleasure in eating food.
 
 
• **Example:** He relished the food served at the grand banquet.
 
 
 
• **Encourage starvation** (भुखमरी को प्रोत्साहित करना): To support or promote a state of not having enough food to eat.
 
 
• **Example:** Their cruel policies seemed to encourage starvation among the poor.
